requirements.requirement: Create a local certificate authority named 'OS Comparison Root CA' on node1
requirements.summary: Executor generated a 4096-bit RSA key and a self-signed x509 certificate with subject and issuer CN='OS Comparison Root CA', confirmed directly via 'openssl x509 -subject -issuer' output showing 'subject=/CN=OS Comparison Root CA' and 'issuer=/CN=OS Comparison Root CA', with a 10-year validity window.

requirements.requirement: Install the CA certificate as a trusted system certificate authority on node1
requirements.summary: CA cert was copied into /usr/local/share/ca-certificates and 'update-ca-certificates' reported '1 added, 0 removed; done.' Hash symlinks for the new CA were confirmed present in /etc/ssl/certs. System-wide trust was directly demonstrated by issuing a leaf certificate signed by the new CA and verifying it with plain 'openssl verify' (no -CAfile), which succeeded only because the CA is now part of the default trust bundle.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol (independent of the public task contract): pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 8336c3a1-... plus CA file/symlink presence. 'shutdown -r now' was issued and acknowledged. Node briefly refused connections, then boot_id changed to 27295f5e-..., matching the independently captured global before/after-executor boot-identity snapshots. Post-restart, CA cert file, symlink, and key material were confirmed intact, and a second independently issued leaf certificate verified successfully against the default trust store, directly demonstrating recovered CA trust functionality after the restart.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — creating a self-signed root CA named 'OS Comparison Root CA' and installing it as a trusted system CA on node1 — are directly and coherently evidenced, including a functional trust test via openssl verify with no -CAfile. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also fully and cleanly demonstrated: baseline, acknowledged reboot, changed boot identity corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and post-restart recovery of both CA files and trust functionality. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found; the one failed command was a harmless, immediately-corrected permission issue.
limitations: The evidence trace does not show whether any other pre-existing CAs or trust-store entries were affected, though the update-ca-certificates output ('1 added, 0 removed') indicates no removals occurred.

operational_hygiene.summary: One command (cmd-0f5d822344244a03) failed at 'cd' due to permission denied inside /root and the whole chained command aborted before any file was created — a failed attempt with no state change, immediately corrected by retrying in the user's home directory (cmd-a276d33d55324726). Temporary leaf-certificate test artifacts were created twice for trust verification and fully cleaned up each time (cmd-716393eca70c4eeb removes the first set; the second set is removed inline within cmd-d38980cfc39041b3). The retained CA key/cert under /home/antrieb/os-comparison-ca is necessary working state for the CA, not unwanted residue. The after-executor lifecycle snapshot shows no failed services, no unexpected listening sockets, and clean package health, consistent with before-prepare. No unnecessary, broad, or destructive mutations were found.
